PullRequest.Title: Open side chat, /btw and /fork chats in the chat window they were started from
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #347086

Ask in Side Chat, `/btw` and `/fork` started from a chat window created their new chat in the main Agents window. A new chat was only routed to a chat window's opener when the new chat itself was already shown there (or, for the tool origin, via `_showChatToSide`), so side chat, `/btw` and fork chats fell into the main grid.

## Changes

- `SessionsService`: a new chat opened with a reference chat that a chat window shows now goes to that window's opener (`openBeside`), for every origin. The main grid's `splitChatToSide` is skipped in that case. The lookup is the small shared helper `_getOpenerShowingReference`. If the reference is no longer shown, it falls back to the existing main-grid path. Main-window behavior is unchanged.
- Side chat / `/btw` (`sideChatOrchestration.ts`) and chat/parent-session fork (`agentHostForkActions.ts`) pass the source chat as `referenceChatResource`.
- A side chat from a chat window is sent with the awaited background send. A foreground send discards the main window's new-session draft and makes the main window follow the sent chat, which this route must not do. The main-window path still splits and sends in the foreground.
- `SESSIONS.md`: documents the reference-chat opener rule.

## Reviewer attention

- **Deliberate behavior change:** a tool-origin `openChat` with a reference chat now goes to the reference's chat-host opener (`openBeside`) too, per the "every origin" rule. Please check subagent opens.
- **Follow-up (not in this PR):** forking into a separate session needs new opener API; a unit test documents what it does today.
- Not addressed here: the other window-targeting issues (#347106, #347171, #347091, #347087, #347102).
- Closing the chat window after the opener is chosen is unchanged generic behavior; the submitted side chat stays reachable from the session's chat list.

## How to test

1. Open an Agents window and a chat window for a session.
2. In the chat window, run `/btw <question>`, `/fork`, or select text and use Ask in Side Chat. The new chat opens beside the source in the chat window, not in the main window.
3. Before step 2, type a draft in the main window's new-session composer: it is still there afterwards.

Validation on the head commit:
- `pnpm run typecheck-client`: passed
- `pnpm run valid-layers-check`: passed
- `pnpm run eslint` on the changed files: passed
- `scripts/test.sh --runGlob "vs/sessions/**/test/**/*.test.js"` (Electron): 8202 passing
- `npm run test-browser-no-install -- --runGlob "vs/sessions/**/test/**/*.test.js" --browser chromium`: 7958 passing
- `vs/workbench/contrib/sessions/**`: one failing test, PromptTemplatePlaceholderController (known, unrelated, pre-existing on main)
- Live: before/after of `/btw` and `/fork` from a chat window in a throwaway profile, plus `/btw` with a seeded main-window draft that survived. Not covered live: the Ask in Side Chat selection UI and the separate-session fork.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create and send a side chat from an existing chat window
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The provider must create the side chat, openChat must resolve the session and open the new chat beside the reference in the existing chat window, and the provider send must complete. All remain awaited before the command resolves.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke the selected sessions provider to create one side chat, potentially crossing to its backend.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one provider create call per side-chat action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same provider create call was awaited before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before the new chat can be opened or sent.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Ask each provider that supports resource resolution to resolve the session resource, sequentially until one claims it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one call per resolving provider for the single open; unchanged and typically a small provider set.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: openChat already performed the same resolution before this change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before either grid or chat-window routing occurs.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open one chat editor beside the reference in its existing chat window.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One open per action after a bounded opener lookup; no per-chat opens.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The new chat instead followed the main-grid open path; this replaces that UI work rather than adding a second open.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Submit one request through the selected sessions provider/backend.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one send per side chat.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The foreground path invoked the same provider.sendRequest once; the diff only sets background semantics and suppresses navigation listeners.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The orchestration awaits provider completion in both old and new paths.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One explicit side-chat action. Opener discovery scales with the number of open chat-window contents/chats/editor groups; there is one registered production opener and no collection-wide boundary fan-out.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One create, one open, and one send are serialized for each user action. The background send changes follow/navigation semantics but still awaits the same single provider send; no burst or new parallelism is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new cache is introduced or bypassed. Session/provider state and opener contents are live in-memory lookups; cold and warm behavior have the same boundary cardinality.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed call path and all awaited operations are directly visible in the orchestration, SessionsService, opener service, and chat-window opener implementation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider and editor-open latency depends on backend and window state, but their call counts are fixed at one and the diff replaces grid routing rather than stacking work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The changed route avoids activating the main grid and performs one existing-window editor open; provider create/send counts and serialization are unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create and send a side chat from the main sessions grid
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Create the chat, resolve/open it in the grid, split it to the side, and send through the provider.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create one side chat through the sessions provider.
Resolve the session through providers supporting resolution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One sequential pass for the single open.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Submit one request to the provider/backend.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One user action; the added reference lookup scans the in-memory opener collection and chat-window contents once after the target lookup. It does not scale with session history or cause boundary calls.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The operations remain serialized and user-triggered, with one provider send. No new concurrent work is scheduled.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No changed cache behavior. If no chat window owns the grid reference, the lookup misses in memory and proceeds through the prior grid path.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the sourceInGrid branch preserves split and foreground-send behavior, and the opener implementation establishes the lookup cardinality.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: A user can open multiple chat-window chats/groups, increasing the in-memory showsChat scan, but this occurs once per explicit action and has no realistic high-frequency trigger.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The only added work is one bounded in-memory ownership lookup on a human-triggered path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Fork a chat within a multi-chat session from the grid or a chat window, including open-to-side
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The provider fork must finish, then SessionsService resolves the resource and opens the fork either in the grid or beside the source in its chat window.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fork one chat through the selected agent-host sessions provider/backend.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one fork call per command, independent of request-history size after the local turn lookup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same fork call occurred before routing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must finish before the fork can be opened.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the fork's session resource through applicable providers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One sequential resolution pass for one fork open.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Both openChat and openChatToSide already resolved the resource.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open the fork beside its source when the source is hosted by a chat window.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Non-tool forks fell through to one grid open; tool-origin open-to-side already used this opener route. The diff substitutes the host route for the grid route.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One explicit fork command. History is scanned once locally to locate the source turn, as before; routing adds at most one in-memory reference-owner lookup.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One fork and one open are serialized per command. No Promise.all, queue expansion, or per-history-item fan-out is added.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new cache or retention. Opener ownership is queried live so closed windows naturally miss and fall back to the existing grid route.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: fork provider invocation, routing branches, opener lookup, and tests all establish one-for-one replacement behavior.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Backend fork duration is provider-dependent, but unchanged. Editor-open costs differ between grid and chat window, with no evidence that the substituted existing-window route is more expensive.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Boundary cardinality is unchanged, and the new reference routing replaces rather than adds UI opening work.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all seven changed files and all diff pages. Traced side-chat and fork creation, session resolution, opener lookup, chat-window opening, and request sending. The PR adds only bounded in-memory ownership checks and substitutes existing-window routing/background navigation semantics without increasing provider boundary counts, concurrency, retained state, or hot-path work. No valid performance findings or regression-fix learning signal.
